description: Implementation of a high-performance timer management system with timer wheel, supporting create, start, stop, destroy, and expiry callbacks, using lock-free queues and intrusive linked lists for efficient timer handling.

classes.name: cmd_t
classes.description: Represents commands for timer control: start, stop, create, destroy.

classes.name: timer_update_signaller
classes.description: Handles batching and signaling of timer update commands between front-end and back-end.

classes.name: backend_channel
classes.description: Channel for communication of timer commands from front-end to back-end, with overwrite semantics.

classes.name: frontend_handle
classes.description: Represents a timer instance on the front-end, managing its state and callbacks.

classes.name: timer_manager::manager_impl
classes.description: Core implementation of the timer manager, managing timer wheel, creation, deletion, and expiry handling.

classes.name: timer_handle
classes.description: Holds front-end and back-end context for each timer.

methods.name: handle_timer_commands
methods.description: Processes queued timer commands each tick.

methods.name: try_stop_timer_backend
methods.description: Attempts to stop a timer, handling expiry if needed.

methods.name: trigger_timeout_handling
methods.description: Dispatches expiry callback to the timer's executor.

methods.name: handle_postponed_timeouts
methods.description: Retries timeout callbacks that failed previously.

methods.name: create_frontend_timer
methods.description: Creates or reuses a front-end timer handle.

methods.name: tick
methods.description: Advances the timer system by one tick, processing expiries.

methods.name: set
methods.description: Sets timer duration and optional callback.
